A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NOBLE research and contain 26 readable pages, including Appendices A–F. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original PVALB and VIP neuron prediction experiments, comparisons with experimental recordings, ablations, fine-tuning results, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including the numerical evaluations in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The FNO architecture, frequency-modulated embeddings, training losses, and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Section 4.1 corrects and consolidates the input description without establishing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PVALB and VIP neurons with square-step current inputs, held-out HoF models, and synthetic models sampled through latent-space interpolation. No dataset, population, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain HoF/PDE simulations, interpolation between PDE parameterizations, and experimental recordings. The newly cited FNO explanatory paper is not an additional evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The 50/10 HoF split, 75,600 training samples, training budgets, current stimuli, and relative L4 training and L2 evaluation metrics are retained. The 50-model neighborhood interpolation protocol was already described in v3.

E4.justification: The embedding ablation, subsampling sensitivity study, HoF-diversity analysis, and feature-specific fine-tuning analysis are retained. The ensemble analysis used in the revised Figure 4C already appeared in Appendix D.5 and Figure 13.

E5.justification: The IQR displays in Figure 5 and mean, standard-deviation, and minimum–maximum reporting in Figures 6–7 remain unchanged. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: The specific voltage traces previously reported in Figure 4C are replaced by different traces matching the ensemble already shown in Figure 13. This replaces one illustrative result; tabulated scores, reported error rates, speedups, and overall findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The embedding definition, neural-operator equations, relative-error definition, and feature-specific loss formulations are mathematically unchanged. Differences in mathematical spacing and typesetting do not alter their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning biologically informed embeddings, neuronal variability, interpolation, experimental validation, and the 4200-fold inference speedup.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 now interprets Figure 4C specifically as agreement with a previously unseen HoF/PDE model, where v3 described agreement with experimental recordings. Agreement with experimental observations is instead tied explicitly to Figure 4A. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies that the PDE F-I comparison uses slightly perturbed parameterizations of the held-out HoF model, refining the earlier generic interpolation description. This adds procedural detail without establishing a changed experiment; hyperparameters, hardware, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds Duruisseaux, Kossaifi, and Anandkumar's Fourier Neural Operators Explained: A Practical Perspective as reference 30, cited in the introduction, Section 3.3, and Appendix C.3. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 receive localized rewriting that clarifies input attribution and organizes the interpolation explanation. Other wording and bibliographic edits are limited; section order and appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4C is redrawn using the ensemble already displayed in Figure 13. Captions for Figures 3, 4, 5, and 11 receive corrections or clarifications, with minor local reflow. The figure inventory and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 improves clarity and consistency by correctly attributing embedding inputs to NOBLE in Section 4.1 and explaining the held-out PDE comparison and ensemble predictions more accurately in Figure 4 and Section 4.3. Existing appendix evidence becomes clearer in the main text. These are limited improvements; experimental breadth, quantitative validation, and stated limitations remain essentially unchanged.
